newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Plan to cut Portugal civil service pensions - paper.
newsitem.headline: Plan to cut Portugal civil service pensions - paper.

text.p: A white paper to be considered by the Portuguese government proposes cutting civil service pensions, Diario de Noticias newspaper reported.
It said that under the proposals, which will be formally presented next week, civil servants would no longer receive pensions equivalent to 100 percent of their final salary.

The paper quoted sources involved in the process as saying that civil servants would receive at best a pension equivalent to 80 percent of their average salary in the highest-paying 10 of the last 15 years of service.
It also said that civil servants would have to serve an additional four years to qualify for the maximum pension, which means a career lasting 40 years.
"The state, with depleted coffers, could not give itself the luxury of giving workers 100 percent of final salary," one source told the paper.
Like other European countries, Portugal is struggling to meet commitments to its state pensions system as it is under pressure from an ageing population.
Government officials were not immediately available to comment on the newspaper report.
